messages:
Evelyn (AcmeCo): Hey team — our March invoice shows ~1.2M tokens but the project dashboard shows ~900k for the same period. Also saw intermittent 429s yesterday even though the project tile indicated available quota. Can someone look? Project: acme-web-prod, org: AcmeCo. Sample request-id: req_3f9a2b.

Maya (Support): Sorry to hear that — can you confirm the exact timestamps for the invoice window and a couple more request IDs? Did the 429s happen at specific times? Also any screenshots would help. :eyes:

Evelyn (AcmeCo): Invoice period is 2026-03-01..2026-03-31. More req ids: req_3f9a2b, req_3f9a9c, req_3fb12e. 429s around 2026-03-30 23:40-23:55 UTC. Dashboard export shows 898,743 tokens for the project during March. Invoice ledger shows 1,204,112 tokens.

Maya (Support): thanks. I'm escalating to billing + eng-sre. @Dan (Billing) @Ravi (Eng-SRE) — initial hypothesis: late ingestion/backfill or double-counting between org-pool and project aggregation.

Dan (Billing): looking at invoice generation logs now. There was a backfill run on 2026-04-01 that processed >300k late metering events stamped in March but ingested after midnight. Invoice pipeline uses event_time bucketed by month; dashboard realtime tiles use processed_time for rolling windows. That mismatch could cause the dashboard to appear lower while invoice includes late events.

Ravi (Eng-SRE): good lead. Another angle — enforcement (429) is applied against the rolling-window token counter which uses processed_time and shard attribution. If the backfill changed processed_time ordering, it can affect the rolling-window enforcement but not the visible project tile which reads pre-aggregated tiles cached hourly. TL;DR: two different time semantics.

Claire (Eng): I pulled the metering-receiver logs for the sample req ids. There's evidence of duplicate ingestion attempts for a small subset due to a retry storm from a partner connector on 2026-03-30. Example log snippet:

```
metering-receiver[pid=1223] INFO received event {request_id: "req_3f9a2b", event_id: "evt_0x7c1", tokens: 512}
metering-receiver[pid=1223] WARN duplicate event? dedup-key missing for evt_0x7c1
ingest-worker[pid=44] INFO wrote metering_row (event_id=evt_0x7c1, processed_at=2026-04-01T00:12:03Z)
```

Claire (Eng): looks like the backfill ingested duplicates for ~12k events; combine that with the scheduled monthly backfill (which replays event_time) and we get the ~300k delta Dan saw.

Dan (Billing): reconcile query I ran (high-level):

```
-- compare ledger vs dashboard aggregation
SELECT month(event_time) as m, sum(tokens) as ledger_tokens
FROM invoice_ledger
WHERE org_id='acme'
AND month(event_time)=3
GROUP BY 1;

SELECT month(processed_time) as m, sum(tokens) as dashboard_tokens
FROM realtime_tiles
WHERE project_id='acme-web-prod'
AND month(processed_time)=3
GROUP BY 1;
```

Dan (Billing): ledger_tokens = 1,204,112; dashboard_tokens = 898,743. The delta maps to late ingests and ~12k duplicated events.

Ravi (Eng-SRE): For the 429s at 2026-03-30 23:40-23:55 UTC I checked enforcement logs. Enforcement decision used processed_time window which temporarily included some earlier events processed by a different shard, causing a sawtooth in the rolling counter. Enforcement saw the counter cross threshold -> returned 429s. Project tile (cached) hadn't been updated yet so it still showed available.

Maya (Support): So root causes are: 1) backfill run that re-ingested events with March event_time but processed in April (invoice picks them up, dashboard doesn't); 2) a small duplicate ingestion (retry storm) adding ~12k tokens; 3) rolling-window enforcement uses processed_time leading to transient 429s when processed order changes. Is that right?

Claire (Eng): Yup. Suggested immediate mitigations:
- disable the monthly backfill until we add an event dedup index and make backfill idempotent.
- add a reconciliation job to detect late-event deltas > X% and flag for review before invoice finalize.
- short-term fix for enforcement: use event_time for rolling-window counters (safer) or at least a grace window for processed-time anomalies.

Dan (Billing): For the customer: we can offer a provisional credit for the duplicated tokens (12,345 tokens) today and follow-up after a full reconciliation. If backfill is causing >5% delta we should consider crediting the rest. I'll open a billing case and propose a credit line item referencing invoice INV-2026-03-ACME.

Evelyn (AcmeCo): Thanks — appreciate the quick triage. Will you also share what we can do to avoid this from our side?

Maya (Support): Two quick customer-side suggestions: 1) enable org-level usage export so you can cross-check ledger vs dashboard nightly (we can help enable), 2) if you rely on strict quota enforcement, consider switching the project to Dedicated capacity or increasing burst limits during month-end ETL windows.

Ravi (Eng-SRE): Also temporary workaround to avoid 429 surprises: set enforcement policy to prefer org-pool fallback (config flag org_pool_prefer=true) so requests degrade to org pool rather than hard 429 when project counters fluctuate.

Dan (Billing): I'll attach a draft credit memo and the reconciliation queries in the billing case.

Maya (Support): Next steps: 1) Claire/Eng to disable backfill and add dedupe (ETA 48h), 2) Dan to issue provisional credit and create billing ticket, 3) Ravi to patch enforcement semantics or add grace window (ETA 72h), 4) Support to enable org-level export for AcmeCo and keep customer updated.

Evelyn (AcmeCo): Sounds good. Please keep me posted — we rely heavily on cost predictability. :+1:
